title: AI-enhanced full stack SaaS platform
summary: Took an AI-enhanced SaaS product from an early MVP to production as the founding engineer.
context: Joined a startup as technical lead to build a knowledge-management platform. Small codebase, no infrastructure, an aggressive timeline — every architectural decision was mine to make and own.
highlights: Architected and built the full stack: a React / Next.js frontend, a Hono RPC backend, and PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM.
Stood up the entire cloud setup on Hetzner Cloud with Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing.
Integrated LLM features end to end with the AI SDK, designing the prompt flows and streaming UX.
Adopted an AI-first workflow for code review, refactoring, and rapid iteration on complex features.

title: Angular migration
summary: Led the frontend modernization of a business-critical .NET WebForms application to Angular.
context: An enterprise aviation client ran a business-critical application on aging .NET WebForms. I was brought in to define and lead the migration to a modern Angular frontend.
highlights: Defined the migration strategy and target architecture for the new Angular frontend.
Drove the key technical decisions and set the patterns the team built on.
Prioritized technical excellence and performance from the start.

title: Streamlining Code Review
summary: Owned high-impact features on Google's internal code review platform, used by 80,000+ developers.
context: Part of a small, high-impact team maintaining the code review platform behind Google's entire engineering org. The features we owned directly shaped global developer productivity and satisfaction.
highlights: Led data-driven product improvements by analyzing user behavior patterns.
Improved IDE integration and measurably reduced review friction.
Optimized workflows through iterative, measured changes.
outcome: The improvements contributed to 25+ SWE-years of annual productivity savings across the org.

title: Code Review IDE Integration
summary: Brought code review artifacts directly into Google's internal VS Code–based IDE.
context: Integrated code review artifacts into Google's internal IDE (VS Code based), so developers could act on the comments they receive on their code without ever leaving their editor.
highlights: Designed and built the in-IDE code review integration.
Planned each feature in close coordination with UX research.
Rolled out gradually while monitoring performance and satisfaction across 80k+ users.

title: Insurance Calculator
summary: A public-facing health-insurance calculator where users configure and price their own coverage.
context: Visana needed an online calculator that lets users browse and assemble their individual health insurance — essentially a large, high-stakes form where input validation is everything.
highlights: Built the calculator front to back, with validation as a first-class concern.
Worked in a Scrum team, taking part in feature planning and execution.
Backed the frontend with a Java / Spring Boot service.

title: SBB Ticket Terminal Modernization
summary: Rebuilt the ticket-machine interface used across Switzerland's 1,000+ self-service rail terminals.
context: In a team of fewer than 10, we rebuilt the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) ticket vending machine interface — software that serves millions of passengers and must run unattended, 24/7, on terminals nationwide.
highlights: Architected and owned the state machine logic for payment processing, ticket printing, and transaction workflows.
Engineered for fault-tolerant, 24/7 unattended operation across 1,000+ terminals.
Collaborated with disability advocacy organizations throughout the development lifecycle.
Built the UI for performance and failure tolerance on resource-constrained terminals where peripherals and network paths can fail mid-transaction.

title: Custom Tracking Library
summary: A GDPR-compliant, Google-free analytics library that became a core SBB dependency.
context: To stay GDPR-compliant and independent of Google's tracking, we built a cross-browser library to track user behavior and displayed content. It grew into a necessary dependency across the SBB website, so extremely broad browser and version compatibility was non-negotiable.
highlights: Built a failure-tolerant tracking library, published it to npm, and shipped it as a core dependency across the SBB website.
Targeted every browser on every device — legacy versions included — where broad compatibility was non-negotiable.
Backed that bar with TDD, a large suite of unit and UI tests, and extensive real-device validation on BrowserStack.

title: Mobile Security Training Quiz
summary: A playful, lightly competitive quiz that trains colleagues on security topics.
context: A mobile-first, card-based quiz that lets teams learn security topics playfully — with a competitive edge between colleagues. Built in a small team of fewer than 10 and sold to companies as a training product on Microsoft AppSource.
highlights: Oversaw team progress and helped plan the feature roadmap.
Shaped the playful, competitive mechanics that make the training stick.
Coordinated communication and discussion with the UI team.

title: Technological Research in AR & VR
summary: An AR prototype that lets maintenance workers read a factory's status at a glance.
context: A technological research project: an AR prototype to oversee and maintain factory conveyor belts. A digital overlay signals the status of each component, giving a maintenance worker an immediate read on the state of the whole facility.
highlights: Built the AR overlay that surfaces real-time component status.
Designed it to give maintenance workers an at-a-glance facility overview.
Ran a user study measuring performance and user confidence.
outcome: The study showed that user response time and confidence both improved significantly with the overlay.

title: Car Interior Control System Prototype
summary: An exploratory Android app to control vehicle interior functions from a phone.
context: Exploratory development of an Android app to control interior vehicle functionality, exploring how it could be made more helpful and satisfying to use.
highlights: Reverse-engineered an existing control app to understand its behavior.
Re-bundled and reorganized its functionality to improve usefulness and satisfaction.

title: Smart Home Control
summary: Built the full frontend of a Cordova smart-home app designed to help elderly people live independently.
context: KundoXT was building a smart-home system aimed at supporting elderly people in their daily lives. The companion app — Angular 2 on Apache Cordova — let users view and control their smart-home features across devices. I joined a small team of fewer than 10 to build out the frontend.
highlights: Built the entire frontend in Angular, with only minor help.
Displayed and controlled the home's smart features through a cross-platform Cordova app.
Designed the experience around an elderly, accessibility-minded audience.
outcome: The smart-home product the app controls was released to customers a few months later.

title: In-Car VR Experience Prototype
summary: An in-car VR prototype driven by live vehicle data — an early take on what later became holoride.
context: Researched and built an exploratory in-car VR experience powered by live vehicle data. The work spanned everything from gathering test data to building a test environment so features could be validated outside the car. In-car VR is prone to nausea and vertigo, which made user acceptance the central question.
highlights: Piped live vehicle data into the experience via C++ transformations, with the main program in C# / Unity.
Built a test environment to develop and validate features outside the vehicle.
Focused user testing on comfort, nausea, and vertigo to gauge acceptance of the concept.
